report.verdict: A record Q3 top line (€83.1m / ~$91.2m, +6% organic) and a 39% North American EBITDA margin are genuine, but they were earned while absorbing a €6.5m (~$7.1m) sports-win-margin shortfall, a one-third collapse in Europe & RoW EBITDA, and a Brazilian ban that removes ~€30m (~$33m) of annual revenue from Q4 onward with no 2027 framework to replace it. Guidance was "maintained" only because it was already cut in September; the shares fell 9% to SEK 57.90, a fresh 52-week low.

summary: **Record Q3, in line with the September reset but light versus brokers.** Revenue €83.1m (~$91.2m), +6.2% reported, +6% organic, +5% in constant currency; EBITDA before special items (bsi) €21.9m (~$24.0m), +6.1%, margin 26.3% (unchanged YoY, down from 30.3% in Q2). Redeye described the print as below its forecasts on a soft sports-win margin and higher direct costs; we could not locate a formal consensus [unverified].

**Luck masked ~€6.5m of earnings.** Management quantifies the unusually low sports-win margin as a €6.5m (~$7.1m) hit to both revenue and EBITDA versus a normal margin; because Q3-25 was a record-low quarter (-€10m), the YoY effect is nil. Normalised, Q3 EBITDA bsi would have been ~€28m at a ~32% margin. Q2-26 enjoyed a ~€3m tailwind, so the QoQ swing from luck alone is ~€9.5m — most of the €6.0m QoQ revenue decline. On the call management conceded margins have been below normal in four of the last five quarters.

**Revenue bridge: ~€8m of underlying growth absorbed ~€3m of tax/regulatory drag.** Underlying growth ~€8m (incl. ~€1m FX tailwind) from talent-led media, sponsorship, prediction markets, Playbook and HLTV; less ~€2m from the UK Remote Gaming Duty rise (21%→40% from 1 Apr 2026) and ~€1m from Brazil. Net: +€4.9m.

**Guidance 'maintained' = the 27 Sep cut stands; Brazil is the whole story.** FY26 organic revenue growth 3-8% and EBITDA bsi growth -7% to +3% (both constant currency), versus the original 7-12% and 8-18%. The downgrade sits entirely in Europe & RoW (Publishing and Paid Media in Brazil): FY26 Brazil revenue now ~€30m (~$32.9m) vs ~€45m (~$49.4m) planned, a ~€15m (~$16.5m) hit concentrated in Q4. 2027-28 financial targets (which included a 35-40% EBITDA bsi margin ambition) were withdrawn and the €40m FY26 buyback programme discontinued after €23m (~$25.2m) executed.

**Implied Q4 (our arithmetic, constant currency):** revenue €85-102m vs Q4-25 €94.3m (-10% to +8%); EBITDA bsi €24-34m vs €36.9m (-35% to -8%), midpoint ~€29m at ~31% margin. Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter (NFL, European football), so even the top of the range implies a YoY profit decline.

**North America is now the P&L.** Revenue +28% to €26.6m (~$29.2m), EBITDA bsi €10.3m (~$11.4m) vs €3.3m, margin 39% vs 16% (Q2: 26%). TTM NA revenue €108m (~$118m), +19% reported / +26% cc after a ~€5.5m FX headwind. NA is 32% of group revenue (27%) but 47% of group EBITDA bsi (16%). Sponsorship +112%, CPA +39% on prediction-market partners; revenue share -18% against a hybrid-deal comp; subscriptions -9%.

**Europe & RoW is shrinking in profit terms.** Revenue -1.5% to €56.5m (~$62.0m); EBITDA bsi -33% to €11.6m (~$12.7m); margin 20.4% vs 30.1% (-970bps) and 31.9% in Q2. Costs +12% on a flat top line. UK duty, Brazil and the sports margin all land here; the Brazil Q4 hit will compound against a derived Q4-25 comp of ~€63m revenue / ~€19m EBITDA.

**Business lines: Publishing carries growth, Paid Media is the casualty, Esports flattered by timing.** Publishing +16% to €53.9m (~$59.1m), EBITDA bsi +19% to €13.4m, 24.8% margin; Paid Media -12% to €24.2m (~$26.6m), EBITDA bsi -31% to €4.9m, 20.1% margin (-560bps); Esports +14% to €5.0m (~$5.5m), EBITDA bsi +58% to €3.7m, 73% margin (Counter-Strike event-cost timing).

**Mix is shifting away from the annuity.** Sponsorship +66% to €15.9m (~$17.4m), now 18% of revenue (12%); CPA +10% to €20.4m (~$22.4m); revenue share -8% to €35.5m (~$39.0m), 43% of revenue (49%); CPM -16% to €6.4m; subscriptions +12% to €4.4m. Recurring revenue fell to 56% of the total from 64%. From the FY26 annual report sponsorship and CPM will be merged into a single 'Advertising' line — which will obscure the programmatic decline.

**Volume KPIs softening ahead of the Brazil hole.** NDCs 272k (-3% YoY, -27% QoQ after the World Cup), 70% on revenue share, with CPA-based intake rising on NA prediction markets. Value of Deposits €794m (~$871m), +9% YoY but -5% QoQ; management explicitly flags a negative Brazil impact on VoD 'in the coming quarters'.

**Cost base already flexed, with more to come.** Total costs +6% to €61.2m (~$67.2m) but -€1m QoQ; direct costs +16% to €29.3m (35.2% of revenue, +285bps) on World Cup activity, talent-led media and Paid Media campaigns; staff costs -3% with average FTE 1,277 vs 1,513 (-16% YoY, -17% QoQ from 1,535 after the July efficiency measures). Further Brazil-related 'operational adjustments' were made after quarter-end; management would not quantify (Nordea cited a prior Brazil cost base of ~€10m). Special items only €2.1m.

**Below EBITDA the picture is poor.** D&A rose to €13.2m from €9.6m as capitalised talent-led and development projects amortise (9M intangible additions €32.6m vs €1.8m); EBIT bsi -24% to €8.7m (~$9.6m); net financials -€4.0m; ETR 54.5% on unrecognised tax losses; net profit €1.2m (~$1.3m), EPS €0.02 vs €0.03. No adjusted EPS is disclosed.

**Cash flow: headline conversion fine, capex-adjusted less so.** Operating cash flow bsi €26.4m (~$29.0m) vs €34.8m (working-capital timing), 119% conversion; operating cash after interest and tax €19.6m; intangible capex €11.2m (~$12.2m) vs €4.8m. Our FCF estimate (operating CF less intangible/tangible capex): €8.1m (~$8.9m) vs €13.9m in Q3-25; 9M €29.9m (~$32.8m) vs €23.2m.

**Balance sheet: no refinancing risk, modest headroom.** NIBD €253.5m (~$278m), 2.29x LTM EBITDA bsi (2.51x; YE25 2.53x). €319m (~$350m) Nordea/Nykredit club facility extended to Oct-2029 with an €80m accordion; €267m drawn, €55m undrawn, cash €23.2m (~$25.5m), capital reserves €78m (~$86m). Two DKK 550m swaps re-fixed at 2.64%/2.66% to Oct-2029. €34m of deferred/variable media-partnership payments sit outside NIBD (adjusted leverage ~2.6x).

**Impairment overhang of €50-70m (~$55-77m).** Brazil-related domains and customer accounts were not impaired at 30 Sep because Provisional Measure 1,394/2026 is not yet law; if Congress converts it (60-day extension granted 9 Nov; deliberation deadline 4 Mar 2027 per the call), a non-cash charge in that range follows — ~8-11% of €640m equity. Goodwill CGU tests passed with headroom; a +1pt WACC would not trigger impairment.

**Leadership reshuffle — third ELT configuration in roughly two years.** Co-founder Jesper Søgaard becomes sole CEO; co-founder Christian Kirk Rasmussen exits the co-CEO role and the Executive Leadership Team (stays on the Senior Leadership Team for affiliation/performance-marketing projects) about a year after the co-CEO structure was introduced; CFO Flemming Pedersen becomes COO; Dan Bjerregaard (SVP Finance & Global Shared Services) becomes CFO. Note the interim report's management statement is still signed by both co-CEOs.

**Product and partnership pipeline is the bull case.** Playbook (AI betting assistant) won an Affiliate Product Innovation award and integrated Kalshi and then Novig; Prediction Pro launched 19 Oct (Kalshi/Polymarket pricing, US Midterms hub, standalone or add-on to Action Pro); Yahoo Sports partnership; Playmaker HQ's Roommates Show live event sold >10,000 tickets; FUTBIN became an official EA FC 27 partner; HLTV posted record traffic at the Esports World Cup and launched HLTV Brain.

**Thesis read-through.** The structural growth engine — NA talent-led media, direct-sold sponsorship and prediction-market CPA — is real and now margin-accretive. But the legacy European affiliate annuity (revenue share, Paid Media) is being eroded by tax and regulation, and 2027 starts with a ~€30m revenue hole and no guidance. At ~0.5x book and ~SEK 3.3bn market cap the equity is pricing Brazil as permanent and NA as unproven; the FY26 report on 24 Feb 2027 (impairment decision, any 2027 framework) is the next catalyst.

segments.name: North America
segments.headline: Revenue +28% and EBITDA tripled to a 39% margin on sponsorship, prediction-market CPA and maturing revenue-share cohorts — now 47% of group EBITDA, but Q4-25's derived 56% margin is the comp to beat.
narrative: They grew North American revenue 28% to €26.6m (~$29.2m), up 10% sequentially and 24% year-to-date to €76.7m (~$84.1m); on a trailing-twelve-month basis the region is now a €108m (~$118m) business, up 19% reported and 26% in constant currency after a ~€5.5m FX translation headwind from the weaker dollar. The mix tells the story: sponsorship revenue more than doubled to €9.2m (now 34% of regional revenue versus 21% a year ago) on talent-led media — Playmaker HQ, the Roommates Show and the new Yahoo Sports distribution partnership — while CPA rose 39% to €5.5m on prediction-market partners whose deals are structured on upfront CPA terms. CPM grew 28% to €2.9m. Against that, reported revenue share fell 18% to €5.8m because the prior-year quarter included hybrid agreements with an upfront CPA component that have since converted to pure revenue share, and subscriptions slipped 9% to €2.9m, though management flagged a strong September rebound in Action Network's products with the start of the NFL season.

EBITDA before special items reached €10.3m (~$11.4m) against €3.3m a year ago, lifting the margin to 38.9% from 16.0% — a 2,290bps expansion — and from 25.9% in Q2 and roughly 31% in Q1 (derived). Regional costs actually fell 7% to €16.2m, or 61% of revenue versus 84%, which management attributes to maturing pure revenue-share cohorts needing less upfront investment, prediction-market and Playbook contributions, and the operating leverage of premium distribution deals for talent-led content. We note one reconciliation wrinkle that deserves a question to IR: the Publishing business line reports costs up 16% 'driven entirely by higher direct costs associated with the expansion of North American activities', yet the North American geographic segment shows costs down 7%; either the group-level and geographic allocations differ materially or talent-led content costs are partly capitalised (9M intangible additions were €32.6m versus €1.8m), in which case the 39% EBITDA margin is flattered relative to EBITA.

Volume disclosure is not regionalised, but the group-level signal is that the share of CPA-based NDCs rose on North American prediction-market demand, and that NA CPA has risen in every quarter this year (Q1 €5.2m, Q2 €5.1m, Q3 €5.5m, derived). Product milestones were dense: Playbook won an Affiliate Product Innovation award and integrated Kalshi and then Novig; Prediction Pro launched on 19 October (after quarter-end) with Kalshi and Polymarket pricing, proprietary forecasting tools and a 2026 Midterms hub, sold standalone or as an add-on to Action Pro; and the Roommates Show's outdoor live podcast sold more than 10,000 tickets in New York. On the call Søgaard said prediction markets were 'already' driving good growth in North America; we would characterise the stream as still CPA-weighted — less recurring than revenue share and more exposed to partner marketing budgets and to state-level pushback on sports event contracts.

Management gives no regional guidance, but the arithmetic matters for Q4: North America delivered €31.3m of revenue and €17.5m of EBITDA bsi (a 56% margin) in Q4-25 (derived from FY25 less 9M-25 disclosures), so the 39% Q3 margin is not a ceiling but neither is it the peak comp. With North America now 32% of group revenue and 47% of EBITDA bsi, the quarter's group result is effectively a function of this region offsetting Europe. The swing factors for Q4 and 2027 are NFL-season subscription and revenue-share conversion, whether direct-sold sponsorship keeps substituting for programmatic at higher yield, prediction-market CPA pricing as operator competition intensifies, and FX, where a EUR/USD around 1.10 versus ~1.16 a year ago continues to cost translation growth.

segments.name: Europe & Rest of World
segments.headline: Flat revenue, EBITDA down a third and margin -970bps to 20% as UK duty, Brazil and a €6.5m sports-margin shortfall meet +12% cost growth; the Brazil hole opens fully in Q4.
narrative: They reported Europe & RoW revenue down 1.5% to €56.5m (~$62.0m), 13% lower sequentially and only 0.7% higher year-to-date at €181.9m (~$199.6m); the region is now 68% of group revenue versus 73% a year ago. Revenue share — the annuity book — fell 5% to €29.7m, and this is where the €6.5m sports-win-margin shortfall, the ~€2m UK Remote Gaming Duty effect (21% to 40% from 1 April) and the ~€1m Brazil impact mostly landed. CPA edged up 2% to €14.9m, sponsorship rose 29% to €6.7m on HLTV's Esports World Cup traffic and European talent-led formats, subscriptions doubled to €1.5m on Mindway AI, and CPM collapsed 35% to €3.5m as FUTBIN monetisation softened ahead of the EA FC 27 cycle and direct sales cannibalised programmatic.

Profitability deteriorated sharply: EBITDA before special items fell 33% to €11.6m (~$12.7m), taking the margin to 20.4% from 30.1% a year ago and 31.9% in Q2. Regional costs rose 12% to €45.0m — 80% of revenue versus 70% — reflecting the group's €4m increase in direct costs around the World Cup, talent-led media and Paid Media campaigns. Decomposing the €5.7m EBITDA decline, roughly €3m is the UK duty and Brazil, and the balance is cost growth against a flat top line; the sports margin was neutral year-on-year but, had it been normal, the regional margin would have been closer to 29%. In other words the structural damage is running at €3-4m a quarter from tax and regulation, with luck doubling the optical hit this quarter.

Brazil dominates the regional narrative. Revenue there peaked above €70m in 2024, fell to €49m in 2025 after the 1 January regulation and new tax regime, and is now expected at ~€30m (~$32.9m) for 2026 against ~€45m planned before Provisional Measure 1,394/2026 of 25 September banned fixed-odds betting, online casino and related marketing, with operators required to cease by 6 October. The Q3 impact was ~€1m plus softer NDC intake; ~€15m (~$16.5m) of revenue disappears in Q4. Management now plans on zero Brazilian betting and casino revenue, has started cost and organisational adjustments, and declined to quantify the residual cost base (Nordea's analyst referenced a prior figure of ~€10m), saying only that the effect would be 'fully visible in Q4'. Brazil-related domains and customer accounts carry €50-70m of value that will be impaired if the MP is converted into law — Congress granted a 60-day extension on 9 November with a deliberation deadline of 4 March 2027 per the call — and the CEO's letter is unusually blunt in calling the ban counter-productive. The UK is the second regulatory drag: the duty increase is being passed through by operators via tighter CPA and revenue-share terms, and Paid Media's UK casino book is the most exposed.

Disclosure within the region remains thin: there is no split of UK & Ireland, the Nordics, Southern Europe or LatAm ex-Brazil, so the market cannot see whether the ex-Brazil European business is growing at all — a material gap given how much regulatory flux sits here. Esports' cost timing helped (Counter-Strike event promotion phasing cut Esports costs 36%), and HLTV Brain and FUTBIN's official FC 27 status are genuine content assets, but the Q4 set-up is unforgiving: Q4-25 Europe & RoW delivered ~€63m of revenue and ~€19.4m of EBITDA bsi (31%, derived), and Q4-26 must absorb the full Brazil loss. The things to watch are the Value of Deposits trajectory ex-Brazil, whether the sports margin normalises in an NFL- and football-heavy quarter, UK operator terms, Paid Media ROI discipline, and the MP vote — a rejection or lapse would restore a free option on ~€30m-plus of annual revenue that management is explicitly not planning for.

segments.name: Business-model segments: Publishing, Paid Media, Esports
segments.headline: Publishing (+16%) carries the group; Paid Media (-12% revenue, -31% EBITDA) is where UK tax and Brazil bite; Esports' 73% margin is event-timing.
narrative: Publishing, the owned-and-operated media network, grew revenue 16% to €53.9m (~$59.1m), 65% of the group, with organic growth of 16% against -11% a year ago. Sponsorship rose 79% to €12.3m on Playmaker HQ and partner demand for talent-led formats; CPA nearly doubled to €7.0m on North American prediction-market acquisition; subscriptions rose 12% to €4.4m on Mindway AI and a September NFL rebound; revenue share slipped 5% to €24.3m as hybrid agreements converted to pure revenue share; CPM fell 12% to €5.4m as direct sales displaced programmatic. Costs rose 16% to €40.5m, which management attributes entirely to direct costs of North American expansion (and note that most group support-function costs are booked here). EBITDA before special items rose 19% to €13.4m (~$14.7m) at a 24.8% margin, up 50bps year-on-year but down from 29.3% in Q2 and well short of the 32% Publishing margin delivered in FY25 — the sports-margin shortfall explains most of that gap. Publishing contributed 61% of group EBITDA bsi versus 54%.

Paid Media — the performance-marketing arm that buys search, social and third-party inventory and therefore runs at ~80% cost-to-revenue — saw revenue fall 12% to €24.2m (~$26.6m), 29% of the group versus 35%, with CPA down 10% to €13.4m and revenue share down 15% to €10.8m. Management cites the UK casino taxation increase, Brazil's late-quarter developments and the sports margin (which hurts Paid Media's revenue-share book while modestly helping Publishing). Costs were cut 6% to €19.4m through campaign ROI discipline, but EBITDA before special items still fell 31% to €4.9m (~$5.3m) and the margin compressed 560bps to 20.1% (Q2: 26.2%); year-to-date revenue is +1% and EBITDA -3%. This is the segment most exposed to the Brazil marketing ban and to UK operator term renegotiation, and its asset-light flexibility is exactly why management can describe it as 'maintaining solid profitability' while its revenue shrinks — but it is also the clearest evidence that the legacy affiliate model is under structural price pressure.

Esports (HLTV and FUTBIN) grew revenue 14% to €5.0m (~$5.5m): sponsorship rose 32% to €3.5m on HLTV's record Esports World Cup traffic and partner demand, revenue share doubled to €0.5m, but CPM fell 33% to €1.0m on FUTBIN engagement and monetisation headwinds ahead of the EA FC 27 title cycle. Costs dropped 36% to €1.3m because Counter-Strike event promotional spend phased differently across quarters, so EBITDA before special items jumped 58% to €3.7m (~$4.0m) at a 73% margin versus 53% a year ago and 63% in Q2; year-to-date the margin is an unchanged 66%, which is the better guide. Esports is 17% of group EBITDA bsi on 6% of revenue, and the FC 27 partnership and HLTV Brain launch are real engagement assets, but Q4 will carry the deferred event costs.

Across the three lines the mix shift is unambiguous: recurring revenue (revenue share, subscriptions, CPM) fell to 56% of the total from 64%, while CPA and sponsorship rose to 43% from 36%. Management frames this as diversification and improving advertising yield; we would frame it as the annuity shrinking (revenue share -8%, and Brazil will cut it further) while direct-sold advertising — contract-based, cyclical and sensitive to partner marketing budgets — fills the gap. Two reporting points matter for how this is tracked. First, the FY26 annual report will merge sponsorship and CPM into a single 'Advertising' line, which will make the programmatic decline invisible. Second, 9M intangible additions were €32.6m (versus €1.8m) as media-partnership and development projects are capitalised; the resulting amortisation (€11.6m in Q3, +54%) sits below EBITDA bsi, so EBITA (€20.4m, +7%) and EBIT bsi (€8.7m, -24%) give a more complete read on the economics of talent-led media than the 26% EBITDA margin does.

blocks.heading: Publishing
blocks.takeaway: Publishing grew revenue 16% to €53.9m (~$59.1m), 65% of the group, with EBITDA bsi up 19% to €13.4m (~$14.7m) at a 24.8% margin.
points: Organic growth 16% against -11% a year ago; sponsorship rose 79% to €12.3m; CPA nearly doubled to €7.0m on prediction-market acquisition.
Subscriptions rose 12% to €4.4m; revenue share slipped 5% to €24.3m on hybrid conversion; CPM fell 12% to €5.4m as direct sales displaced programmatic.
Costs rose 16% to €40.5m, attributed entirely to direct costs of North American expansion; most group support-function costs are booked here.
Margin up 50bps year-on-year but down from 29.3% in Q2 and well short of the 32% FY25 margin, mostly due to the sports-margin shortfall.
Publishing contributed 61% of group EBITDA bsi versus 54%.

blocks.heading: Paid Media
blocks.takeaway: Paid Media revenue fell 12% to €24.2m (~$26.6m) and EBITDA bsi fell 31% to €4.9m (~$5.3m), with margin down 560bps to 20.1%.
points: Segment is 29% of group versus 35%; CPA down 10% to €13.4m, revenue share down 15% to €10.8m; runs at ~80% cost-to-revenue.
Management cites the UK casino taxation increase, Brazil's late-quarter developments and the sports margin, which hurts Paid Media's revenue-share book.
Costs cut 6% to €19.4m through campaign ROI discipline; Q2 margin was 26.2%; year-to-date revenue +1% and EBITDA -3%.
Most exposed segment to the Brazil marketing ban and UK operator term renegotiation; clearest evidence the legacy affiliate model is under structural price pressure.

blocks.heading: Esports
blocks.takeaway: Esports revenue grew 14% to €5.0m (~$5.5m) and EBITDA bsi jumped 58% to €3.7m (~$4.0m) at a 73% margin driven by event-cost timing.
points: Sponsorship rose 32% to €3.5m on HLTV's record Esports World Cup traffic; revenue share doubled to €0.5m; CPM fell 33% to €1.0m on FUTBIN headwinds ahead of EA FC 27.
Costs dropped 36% to €1.3m on Counter-Strike event promotional phasing; margin was 53% a year ago and 63% in Q2.
Year-to-date margin is an unchanged 66%, the better guide; Q4 will carry the deferred event costs.
Esports is 17% of group EBITDA bsi on 6% of revenue; FC 27 partnership and HLTV Brain launch are real engagement assets.

blocks.heading: Mix shift
blocks.takeaway: Recurring revenue fell to 56% of the total from 64%, while CPA and sponsorship rose to 43% from 36%; we see the annuity shrinking.
points: Management frames this as diversification and improving advertising yield.
Revenue share fell 8%, and Brazil will cut it further, while direct-sold advertising, contract-based, cyclical and budget-sensitive, fills the gap.

blocks.heading: Reporting points
blocks.takeaway: The FY26 annual report will merge sponsorship and CPM into one 'Advertising' line, making the programmatic decline invisible; EBITA and EBIT bsi give a fuller read.
points: 9M intangible additions were €32.6m (versus €1.8m) as media-partnership and development projects are capitalised.
Resulting amortisation (€11.6m in Q3, +54%) sits below EBITDA bsi; EBITA €20.4m (+7%) and EBIT bsi €8.7m (-24%) better reflect talent-led media economics than the 26% EBITDA margin.

highlights.text: **North America margin step-change.** EBITDA bsi €10.3m (~$11.4m) vs €3.3m, margin 39% vs 16% (+2,290bps), on sponsorship +112%, prediction-market CPA +39% and maturing pure revenue-share cohorts; regional costs -7% YoY. TTM revenue €108m (+26% cc). NA is now 47% of group EBITDA bsi.

**Direct-sold advertising is scaling.** Group sponsorship +66% to €15.9m (~$17.4m), 18% of revenue vs 12%; Publishing sponsorship +79%, Esports +32%. Yield improvement from direct sales is replacing programmatic (CPM -16%) at higher margin.

**Underlying growth absorbed ~€3m of tax/regulatory drag and €6.5m of bad luck.** ~€8m of underlying revenue growth; at a normal sports-win margin Q3 EBITDA bsi would have been ~€28m (~$31m) at ~32% margin rather than €21.9m at 26%.

**Balance sheet de-risked ahead of the Brazil hit.** NIBD/EBITDA bsi 2.29x (2.51x); €319m (~$350m) club facility extended to Oct-2029 with €80m accordion, €55m undrawn, €78m capital reserves; swaps fixed at 2.64-2.66%. No refinancing event before the Brazil outcome is known.

**Cost base already flexed.** Average FTE 1,277 vs 1,535 in Q2 (-17% QoQ) after July efficiency measures; staff costs -3% YoY; total costs -€1m QoQ with only €2.1m of special items. Further Brazil-related adjustments post quarter-end.

**Prediction markets moving from pilot to P&L.** Kalshi and Novig live in Playbook (which won an Affiliate Product Innovation award), Prediction Pro launched 19 Oct with Kalshi/Polymarket pricing and a Midterms hub; Publishing CPA +93% is largely this. Yahoo Sports distribution partnership adds reach.

**Esports: HLTV sponsorship +32%, EBITDA bsi +58% at a 73% margin, FUTBIN official EA FC 27 partner.** Margin is flattered by Counter-Strike event-cost phasing (9M margin flat at 66%), but revenue growth of 14% is clean.

lowlights.text: **Brazil: ~€15m (~$16.5m) of Q4 revenue gone, ~€30m FY26 vs €45m planned, zero assumed thereafter.** 2027-28 targets withdrawn, buybacks discontinued, and a €50-70m (~$55-77m) non-cash impairment follows if MP 1,394/2026 becomes law (Congress deadline 4 Mar 2027). Brazil was >€70m of revenue in 2024.

**Europe & RoW EBITDA bsi -33% to €11.6m (~$12.7m), margin -970bps to 20.4%.** Costs +12% on revenue -1.5%; UK duty (~€2m/qtr) and Brazil are permanent, and Q4 faces a derived comp of ~€63m revenue / ~€19m EBITDA.

**Paid Media revenue -12%, EBITDA bsi -31%, margin 20.1% (-560bps).** UK casino tax pass-through and Brazil's marketing ban hit the performance-marketing model first; this is the segment most exposed to both.

**The annuity is shrinking.** Revenue share -8% to €35.5m (~$39.0m); recurring revenue 56% of total vs 64%; NDCs -3% YoY and -27% QoQ; Value of Deposits -5% QoQ with management flagging a Brazil drag on VoD in coming quarters.

**Earnings quality below EBITDA.** D&A +37% to €13.2m as capitalised talent/dev projects (9M additions €32.6m vs €1.8m) amortise; EBIT bsi -24%; ETR 54.5%; net profit €1.2m (~$1.3m), EPS €0.02; our FCF estimate €8.1m (~$8.9m) vs €13.9m. €34m of media-partnership liabilities sit outside NIBD.

**Leadership churn and a withdrawn framework.** Co-CEO structure unwound after ~one year; CFO moves to COO and a new CFO installed on the same day guidance beyond 2026 is absent; the interim report is still signed by both co-CEOs. Shares -9% to a 52-week low.

**Disclosure is moving the wrong way.** Sponsorship and CPM to be merged into 'Advertising' from FY26; no regional split inside Europe & RoW despite Brazil/UK flux; Publishing's '+16% costs on NA expansion' does not reconcile with NA geographic costs -7%.

forecast.intro: FY26 guidance is unchanged from the 27 September revision (regulatory release 85/2026), which cut organic revenue growth to 3-8% from 7-12% and EBITDA bsi growth to -7%/+3% from +8%/+18% (both constant currency), withdrew the 2027-28 targets (which had included a 35-40% EBITDA bsi margin ambition for 2027) and discontinued the €40m FY26 buyback after €23m. The entire downgrade is Brazil — i.e. Europe & RoW, split across Publishing and Paid Media — with FY26 Brazil revenue now ~€30m (~$32.9m) versus ~€45m and a ~€15m hit concentrated in Q4; the UK duty rise (~€2m/quarter) was already in the original plan. The net-debt/EBITDA target of <3x is retained. With 9M organic growth at 8% cc and EBITDA bsi +9% cc, the guidance implies Q4 revenue of €85-102m versus €94.3m in Q4-25 and Q4 EBITDA bsi of €24-34m versus €36.9m — a year-on-year profit decline in every scenario, which is what the equity is reacting to.

forecast.view: **Q4-26E (our estimate):** revenue ~€90-93m (~$99-102m), -1% to -4% YoY, as the ~€15m Brazil loss is partly offset by NFL-driven North America, Esports deferred activity and some sports-margin normalisation; EBITDA bsi ~€27-30m (~$30-33m), a 29-32% margin versus 39% in Q4-25, assuming Brazil drops through at ~70% before cost actions. That lands **FY26E revenue ~€349-352m (+4-5% organic cc) and EBITDA bsi ~€101-104m (-1% to +2%), ~29% margin** — low-to-mid guidance on revenue, upper half on EBITDA given 9M is already €74m. **2027E:** the arithmetic starts with a ~€30m revenue hole (~9% of the base) at 60-70% drop-through (-€18-21m EBITDA pre-mitigation), offset by removal of a ~€10m Brazil cost base and by North America compounding at 15-20% on a €108m TTM base (+€16-22m revenue at ~40% incremental margin, +€6-9m EBITDA); net, we see **2027E EBITDA bsi roughly flat to -10% versus FY26E (~€90-105m) before any sports-margin normalisation (worth +€6-7m if Q3-type shortfalls do not recur) and before any Brazil reopening option**. **Leverage:** with buybacks halted and FCF (our definition) of ~€35-40m a year, NIBD should drift to ~€230-240m by end-2027, keeping NIBD/EBITDA at ~2.2-2.6x on that EBITDA range; the 3x ceiling is only threatened if EBITDA bsi falls below ~€80m. The €50-70m impairment is non-cash, outside the EBITDA-based metric, and would cut equity to ~€570-590m. **Margin direction** is down into 2027 at group level (Europe & RoW drag) but up in North America; the stock debate is whether NA's 39% is a run-rate or a seasonal/capitalisation-assisted peak — Q4-25's derived 56% NA margin suggests Q4 can be strong, but Q1-27 will be the first clean read.
watch: Brazil MP 1,394/2026: Congress conversion vote (deadline 4 Mar 2027 per call) and the impairment decision at FY26 results on 24 Feb 2027 — a lapse/rejection restores a ~€30m+ revenue option management is not modelling.
Q4 sports-win margin: a fifth sub-normal quarter in six would raise questions about whether 'normal' has moved as parlay/SGP mix shifts in partners' books.
Value of Deposits and NDC trajectory ex-Brazil in Q4/Q1 — the only external read on the revenue-share annuity.
North America Q4 against a derived 56% margin / €31.3m revenue comp; NFL subscription conversion; prediction-market CPA pricing as operators compete; state-level pushback on sports event contracts.
UK operator CPA/revenue-share terms after the 40% RGD — Paid Media's margin (20%) is the early-warning indicator.
Capitalised intangibles run-rate (~€10-11m/quarter) versus amortisation, and the EBITA/EBIT bsi trend — the honest measure of talent-led media economics.
Whether a 2027 framework is reinstated at FY26 results, the Brazil cost base actually removed, and execution under the sole-CEO/new-CFO structure.
The new 'Advertising' line from FY26 — insist on continued sponsorship vs CPM disclosure.
